title: Connect to MongoDB
idea: Mongoose opens a default connection to MongoDB, and every model uses it. `connectDB` wraps that call so the server starts listening only afterwards.
points: `mongoose.connect(uri, options)` returns a promise that resolves when the connection is open.
`connectDB` reads `MONGO_URI` and sets `dbName` from `DB_NAME`, overriding the URI's database.
`src/index.js` calls `app.listen` only after that promise resolves.
If it rejects, log the error and exit with code 1.

steps.caption: `node src/index.js` starts. The app has not called `listen` yet, so no client can reach it.
`connectDB()` asks Mongoose to connect. The app waits for the promise.
MongoDB accepts. The promise resolves and `connectDB` returns.
Only now does `app.listen` run. Clients reach the app, and its models reach the database.
Second start, but MongoDB is unreachable. The app begins the same way.
The attempt fails. After the timeout you set, the promise rejects.
`.catch` logs the error and calls `process.exit(1)`. `listen` never ran, so no client reaches a half-working app.

code.title: src/db/index.js
code.caption: Lines 5-10 are `connectDB`, saved with `export default connectDB`. The rest connects, then fails on purpose.

walk.text: The database name comes from `constants.js`; here it is inlined so the file runs alone.
`connectDB` reads `MONGO_URI` when called, then awaits the connection.
`dbName` picks the database and overrides any name in the URI.
`serverSelectionTimeoutMS` gives up after 5 seconds. The default is 30, which feels like a hang.
The connection is open: its `name` is `DB_NAME`, and `readyState` 1 means connected.
Disconnect so the script can exit. A running server keeps the connection open.
Nothing listens on that URI, so the promise rejects with `MongooseServerSelectionError`.

code.title: src/index.js
code.caption: The entry point from earlier lessons, now connecting before it listens.

walk.text: `listen` sits inside `.then`, so it runs only after the connection is open.
A rejected connection lands here. The message says why it failed.
Exit with code 1, so scripts and process managers see a failed start.

pitfalls: Set `serverSelectionTimeoutMS`: the 30 second default makes a dead database look like a hang.
Call `listen` only after `connectDB()` resolves: Mongoose queues early queries, then errors after 10 seconds.
Read `MONGO_URI` from the environment; a hard-coded URI ends up in Git.

quiz.why: `dbName` overrides the database named in the URI, so the connection's `name` is `auth-backend`.

takeaway: Connect first, then listen: a server should not start without its database.

starters: What happens to Mongoose queries that run before the connection opens?
Why exit with code 1 instead of letting the server run anyway?
Do I need to close the connection in a running server?
